# West scrambles to fill heavy rare earth gap as China rivalry deepens

By Eric Onstad

November 19, 2025 8:42 AM UTC Updated November 19, 2025

[1/3] Wheel loaders fill trucks with ore at the MP Materials rare earth mine in Mountain Pass, California, U.S. January 30, 2020. REUTERS/Steve Marcus/File Photo Purchase Licensing Rights, opens new tab

- As China limits exports, MP Materials leads US bid for alternatives
- Heavy elements dysprosium and terbium are hard to source
- Brazil emerges as key heavy rare earth ore exporter

LONDON, Nov 19 (Reuters) - The West's push to build a home-grown magnets supply chain to reduce its reliance on China - led by massive U.S. backing for Nevada-based MP Materials - is running into a critical problem: the scarcity of so-called heavy rare earth elements.
